source_caption:
In The Song of Sparrows (2008), directed by Majid Majidi, a quiet story unfolds around an ordinary family trying to get by. Karim, a gentle but struggling father, loses his job at an ostrich farm and travels to Tehran to find work and support his family. Meanwhile, his young son Hussein dreams of raising goldfish in a muddy tank, hoping to turn something simple into a small success.

When the boys finally manage to buy the goldfish, things quickly fall apart. The bucket carrying them starts leaking, slips from their hands, and breaks, sending the fish scattering across the hot pavement. The children rush to save them, but not everything can be saved, and the moment becomes a painful lesson about how fragile hopes can be.

In the end, Hussein releases the surviving fish into a stream instead of trying to profit from them. Karim watches quietly, realizing how much he’s changed while chasing money and survival. The film gently reminds us that sometimes small losses are what bring us back to what really matters.
